products.title: The B Team Top Game: How to Work Against Seated Guards, Supine Guards, and Those Trying to Stand Up by Craig Jones
products.body:
Learn the B-Team top game, including how to work against seated guards, supine guards, and those trying to stand up 

  • Force errors and exploit common mistakes with Craig’s techniques for passing - including stacks, torreandos, leg drags, and more
  • See some of the best ways to clear out of dangerous leg entanglements with leg locking master Craig’s advice
  • Craig is one of the most popular instructors in the world, with ADCC Medals & sustained elite competition success
  • This six-part series will help you understand how to approach and think about playing top in no-gi, and how you can begin to enforce your rhythm and method against your opponents

Redefine No-Gi Guard Passing With Australian Grappling Superstar Craig Jones As He Explains His System For Passing Against Tough Guards And Disengaging Dangerous Positions


What Will You Learn?

See your top game get better than ever with no-gi grappling star Craig Jones’s six-part series on guard passing concepts and techniques that you can use to better your skills. With coaching on how to break down the guard, including how he approaches seated guard, supine guard, and opponents determined to stand up, Craig shows a complete guard passing class for grapplers of all levels.

Use conceptual lessons like how to score your passes through fatigue, and how important the hip pocket is to every pass, as Craig shows you ways to make guard passing a lot simpler through easy adjustments. With drills and techniques built on a strong base of experience in competition against the best, Craig can show you what really works when you want to get to a dominant position and what mistakes people are commonly making.

Craig Jones is one of the most popular grapplers and instructors in the world, with an ADCC medal from 2019 and many elite victories against some of the best in the game. Use Craig’s coaching on leg drags, stacks, torreandos, body locks, and more as he shows you how to approach a dangerous guard and defuse the situation.

Don’t get caught up in those tricky leg entanglements again, Craig explains here on this six-volume series how to avoid those positions and even how to clear from dangerous positions like shin on shin and ashi garami. Combine your techniques into one system with Craig’s help as he shows you all the ways to shut down bottom fighters and be the power top on the mats.

products.title: Power Ride 2.0 by Craig Jones
products.body:
Top half guard is one of the most misunderstood positions in grappling, and few people have turned it into a true pin better than Craig Jones.

  • Craig Jones is a two-time ADCC silver medalist, a black belt under Lachlan Giles and a co-founder of the B-Team, known for breaking down positions in ways nobody else does.
  • In Power Ride 2.0, Jones breaks down his top half guard pinning system: the near side underhook, shutting down the octopus guard, the Quad Lemma setups, and the short darce and head and arm finishes.
  • This isn't just a half guard passing course, it's a complete philosophy on treating top half guard as a pin you can hold, ride and finish from.


What Will You Learn?

Top half guard is one of the most misunderstood positions in grappling, and few people have turned it into a true pin better than Craig Jones.

Craig Jones took silver at ADCC in 2019 and again in 2022, and before that he won the IBJJF No-Gi World Championship as a purple belt. A black belt under Lachlan Giles and a co-founder of the B-Team, he has built his reputation on seeing positions differently from everyone else. Now he's sharing the next chapter of the pinning system he started in the original Power Ride.

Power Ride 2.0 covers the details that make top half guard so hard to escape. You'll learn how to get the near side underhook, ride the hips, kill the bridge and put your opponent in a grey area where they can't recover guard or get out. From there, Jones shows you how to stop the octopus guard, why half guard is the answer, and how to chain the short darce, the kimura, the head and arm choke and the head and arm triangle off the same pin. This isn't just a half guard passing course, it's a complete philosophy on treating top half guard as a pin you can hold, ride and finish from.

Whether you compete in no-gi, train in the gi or just want a more reliable top game, top half guard serves as a home base you can come back to again and again. Jones also shows you how to handle mount when you don't have the underhook, so the system keeps working as the position changes.

The reason it works is simple: instead of rushing to pass, you control the position first and make your opponent carry your weight while you set up your finishes. The Quad Lemma gives you several attacks from one setup, and the live rounds in Volume 5 show you how the whole system holds up against real resistance.

If you've ever wondered why elite grapplers seem happy to stay in top half guard instead of rushing to pass, this course gives you the answer.

Learn how to turn top half guard into a pin your opponents can't escape with Craig Jones.

What Exactly Do You Get?

Part 1: Near Side Underhook

  • NSU Intro
  • Getting the Near Side Underhook
  • Riding the Hips
  • Arguments for NSU
  • Putting Your Opponent in a Grey Area
  • Killing the Bridge
  • Pinning Details
  • Setting Up the Head and Arm Choke
  • NSU Outro

Part 2: Octopus Killer and The Short Darce

  • Octopus Intro
  • Stopping Octopus
  • Why Half Guard Is the Answer
  • What Is Half Guard
  • Short Darce Intro
  • Short Darce Finishing Mechanics
  • Short Darce Outro

Part 3: The Quad Lemma

  • Quad Lemma Intro
  • Setting Up the Pin
  • Islam Makhachev Half Guard Series
  • Kimura Finish
  • Head and Arm Finish
  • Keeping Your Opponent in the Loop

Part 4: Top Half Darce

  • Controlling the Pin
  • Head and Arm Triangle
  • Securing Pin When We Get Greedy
  • Setting Up the Darce
  • Dealing With Mount Without an Underhook
  • Half Guard Is Everywhere

Part 5: Top Half Live Rounds

  • Top Half Live Rounds 1
  • Top Half Live Rounds 2
  • Top Half Live Rounds 3

products.title: Power Ride: A New Philosophy on Pinning by Craig Jones
products.body:
Use Craig’s approach to control to redefine traditional scoring and go beyond points to real control of someone - using this B-Team standard operating procedure

  • Combine upper and lower body controls like the claw, the turk, the half nelson, and more into one grappling-specific riding system that keeps your opponents down
  • Shut down the turtle with the help of Craig’s advice on using spiral rides, underclaws, kosoto hooks, and more for one unified loop
  • Craig is one of the most popular instructors in the world, with ADCC Medals & sustained elite competition success
  • Finish fights with systematic submission attempts from your pinning positions, including arm triangles, rear ezekiels, darces, and more

Control And Dominate Position With B-Team Grappling Star Craig Jones’s 6-Part Series on Holding Down Talented Opponents And Setting Up Fight-Ending Submissions


 

Check out a free sample:

What Will You Learn?

Go beyond points and start learning how to really control someone and hold them down with Australian grappling superstar Craig Jones’s 6-part guide to pinning. With his standard operating procedure, you can get real control and set up fight-ending submission holds without ever sacrificing position.

Learn the best ways to form strong grips and power from top with Craig’s system for applying turks, rear mount, cross faces, claws, and more into upper and lower body controls that all work together. Break down opponents so they can’t get away using these principles and tools for a new grappling arsenal from top position.

Craig Jones is one of the most popular grapplers and instructors in the world, with an ADCC medal from 2019 and many elite victories against some of the best in the game. Now you can learn his formula for dynamically pinning opponents after he has passed the guard - with techniques and concepts that grapplers of all levels can use.

On this six-part series, you’ll get great advice from Craig on how to use some of these control positions to set up submissions, including kimura, darces, arm triangles, and more. These strangles and joint locks will let you get way more taps against your training partners and opponents without ever worrying about giving up control.

So, What Exactly Do You Get?
